subject: Packaging and discounts: observability retention + tracing + dashboards
messages:
From: Alicia Morales <alicia@netlytics.io>
To: grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Tom Reed <tom.reed@netlytics.io>, procurement@netlytics.io
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intro — observability add-ons pricing for Netlytics

Hi Grace —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Netlytics is close to a decision on inference (congrats on the performance numbers) but before we lock in the model capacity we need clarity on the add-ons: retention, tracing, and the advanced dashboard module. Two specific asks from my team: a) a clear tiered pricing table (monthly and annual) and b) an outline of customary discounts for multi-year or committed-volume deals.

High-level context: we expect a steady token ingestion rate of ~10M tokens/day with spikes for batch runs. Tracing retention is important for our SREs — we need 90 days min for full traces with an option for long-term archive. Dashboards will be used by ~12 power users.

Can you send a packaging suggestion + concession playbook so we can prepare an internal procurement request?

Thanks,
Alicia Morales
Head of Platform — Netlytics
Alicia@netlytics.io

--
Attachment: initial-usage-estimates.csv (stub)

From: grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com
To: Alicia Morales <alicia@netlytics.io>
Cc: ben_carter@redwoodinference.com, kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 11:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro — observability add-ons pricing for Netlytics

Alicia —

Appreciate the context, and thanks for sharing the usage file. I put together a concise packaging playbook that maps to three scenarios: Starter (30-day tracing, basic retention), Production (90-day tracing + dashboard seats), and Enterprise (90-day tracing + long-term archive + seat bundle). See the attached pricing-grid.xlsx and a draft SOW (sow-draft.docx).

Quick summary (high level):
- Starter: 30-day trace retention, limited dashboard (up to 5 users), pay-as-you-go retention storage.
- Production: 90-day trace retention, 12 dashboard seats, discounted retention slab (monthly commit).
- Enterprise: 90-day plus archival snapshot, unlimited dashboards with bulk seat discount, 10%–18% discount for 12–24 month commits depending on capacity commit and unit price.

A few notes:
- We typically apply a higher discount to bundled commit vs. stand-alone retention credits.
- Tracing ingestion spikes are covered with a short-burst credit model; long-term archival is priced per GB/month.
- Procurement asks: if you can confirm a 12-month commitment window and expected monthly tokens, I can run numbers with Ben and come back with an approval-ready proposal.

Looping Ben on approvals and Kimberly on billing and commercial packaging details.

Best,
Grace
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
O: 415-555-0142 | grace@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: pricing-grid.xlsx, sow-draft.docx

From: ben_carter@redwoodinference.com
To: grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com, Alicia Morales <alicia@netlytics.io>
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro — observability add-ons pricing for Netlytics

Grace / Alicia —

Thanks for the material, Grace. High level commercial guidance from my side: for a deal like Netlytics (10M tokens/day baseline, SRE emphasis on traces, 12 power users) we can be flexible in the 12%–16% range on aggregate discounts for a 12-month commit if the retention commit is included in the bundle. If Netlytics is willing to agree to a 24-month commit and a modest up-front payment (one monthly invoice upfront), we can push to 18%–22% subject to a simple earnback clause.

Operational concessions we can offer:
- One-time onboarding credit to offset first-month surge (up to $15k).
- Waive the first 30 days of archival storage for Enterprise package pilot.
- 30-day SLA credit for trace retrieval time if they opt into Dedicated capacity.

Kimberly — can you confirm whether the onboarding credit needs legal sign-off or if it is standard for deals under $100k ARR? Also flag any billing quirks for multi-year prepay.

Ben
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
ben@redwoodinference.com

--
(On a separate note: keep the 90-day default for Production but document the archive pricing clearly.)

From: kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com
To: ben_carter@redwoodinference.com, grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Alicia Morales <alicia@netlytics.io>
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro — observability add-ons pricing for Netlytics

Ben / Grace / Alicia —

Confirmed: onboarding credit up to $15k is within standard commercial concessions and does not require additional legal approval for deals under $100k ARR; for >$100k we route a short approval but typical turnaround is 48 hours. Multi-year prepay is supported; billing team needs a note on whether Netlytics wants monthly amortization in invoicing or an annual prepay line. For the pricing-grid.xlsx I recommend we include both per-month-of-commit and effective unit price for the retention GB rate so procurement can compare internally.

Alicia — if you can confirm whether Netlytics prefers amortized monthly billing (recommended for forecasting) or full prepay, we will produce two finalized options in the proposal.

Kimberly Park
Commercial Ops, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com

--
Attachment: billing-ops-notes.pdf (stub)

From: Alicia Morales <alicia@netlytics.io>
To: grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Tom Reed <tom.reed@netlytics.io>, procurement@netlytics.io, ben_carter@redwoodinference.com, kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 31 Jul 2028 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro — observability add-ons pricing for Netlytics

Grace / Ben / Kimberly —

Thanks — this is helpful. Netlytics is inclined to a 12-month commit to start; procurement prefers amortized monthly billing but we can consider an annual prepay if the numbers are compelling. A couple quick clarifications before we take this to the legal team:
1) For the Production bundle, does the 90-day tracing include full-span storage (not just summaries)? We need full-span for root-cause debugging.
2) Is the onboarding credit guaranteed as a one-time invoice credit or applied against first-month usage?
3) Can you include a clear definition of what counts as a "dashboard seat" (admin vs viewer) so we can map our 12 power users correctly.

If you can send a short one-pager that answers these three items along with a final two-option commercial (amortized monthly 12-month commit vs annual prepay with 18% discount), procurement will start the internal approval.

Best,
Alicia
Head of Platform — Netlytics

On Tue, Jul 30, 2028 at 11:07 AM grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com wrote:
> Alicia —
> 
> Appreciate the context, and thanks for sharing the usage file. I put together a concise packaging playbook that maps to three scenarios...

From: grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com
To: Alicia Morales <alicia@netlytics.io>
Cc: ben_carter@redwoodinference.com, kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 31 Jul 2028 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro — observability add-ons pricing for Netlytics

Alicia —

Thanks for the clarifying questions. Short answers below and I will follow up with a one-pager + two-option commercial by EOD.

1) 90-day tracing = full-span retention (request/response and spans) — not just summaries. Production package stores full spans for 90 days; Enterprise archival moves sampled or full spans to cold storage by policy.
2) Onboarding credit: guaranteed one-time invoice credit applied to the first invoice after go-live (we can also apply it as a service credit against professional services if preferred).
3) Dashboard seat definitions: Admin = full configuration and alerting control; Power User = edit dashboards and saved queries; Viewer = read-only. The 12 seats you mentioned map to Power User by default; we can swap up to 3 Viewer seats without changing pricing.

Deliverables: one-pager + pricing-grid (finalized with amortized vs prepay columns) + short SOW with the onboarding credit clause. Expect these in your inbox by 17:00 PT.

Best regards,
Grace
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

--
Attachments sent: pricing-grid.xlsx, sow-draft.docx
